name: fibo_custom
description: Enterprise ontology pack derived from the Enterprise Ontology Reference Guide (Party/Account/Contact/Organization/Sales/Asset domains, FIBO-aligned). DRAFT -- not yet GATE-2 reviewed. Customers are modeled as a Role played by a Party (playsRole -> CustomerRole), never a Person subtype, per the guide's own stated principle. 'Regulator' and 'Custodian' were added as Organization subtypes because the guide's own relationship examples (Organisation -> regulatedBy -> Regulator; BrokerageAccount -> servicedBy -> Custodian) name them as if declared, but no class definition existed for them elsewhere in the guide. Identifier values (LEI, Tax ID, Registration Number, DUNS) are NOT separate entity types -- consistent with fibo_core's convention, LEI is gazetteer-linked external_id metadata on the owning Organization, not its own extractable span.

entity_types.guidance: Any actor participating in business activities.
A natural person.
Any legal entity, company, institution, agency, or organizational unit.
An organization formally registered as a distinct legal person.
An internal organizational division, not a separately registered legal entity.
An internal functional department within an organization.
A pooled investment vehicle (mutual fund, hedge fund, ETF).
A depository, commercial, or investment bank.
A firm that buys/sells securities on behalf of clients or itself.
A firm that manages investment assets on behalf of clients.
A regulatory or supervisory authority (e.g. SEC, FINRA, FCA).
An organization providing custody/safekeeping services for financial assets.
A role a Party plays in a business context -- never a subtype of the Party itself.
The role of being a customer, played by a Person or Organization via playsRole.
A financial or customer-servicing account.
An account for trading securities.
A deposit-taking account (checking, savings).
An account holding assets in custody on behalf of an owner.
An account representing an extended loan/credit facility.
A general investment account.
A channel through which a Party can be reached.
An email address.
A phone number.
A physical or mailing address.
A social media handle or profile identifier.
A binding agreement or contract between parties.
A prospective sales contact not yet qualified as an opportunity.
A qualified, pursuable sales prospect.
The event of a lead converting into a sales opportunity.
Anything of economic value owned by a Party.
A tradable or holdable financial instrument.
Common or preferred stock/shares.
A debt security / fixed-income instrument.
An option, future, swap, or other derivative instrument.
A tangible physical asset (real estate, equipment, commodities).
A digital/intangible asset (e.g. digital currency, IP, software license).

relations.guidance: A party can be reached through a contact point.
A party plays a role (e.g. customer) -- roles are never subtypes.
A person works for an organization.
A party is a member of an organization.
An account is owned by a party.
A party owns an asset or a subsidiary organization.
An account holds a financial asset (equity, bond, derivative).
An account is serviced by an organization (e.g. a custodian).
An organization is regulated by a regulatory authority.
One organization is a subsidiary of another.
A sales opportunity results in a signed agreement.

regex_patterns._comment: ISO 17442 LEI shape (18 alnum + 2 check digits), matches fibo_core's sample (ADR-0013/KG-AC-54). 2026-08-07.
Standard email shape; format-defined, no checksum digit exists for email. 2026-08-07.

dep_patterns._comment: SVO: '<Person> joined/founded <Organization>' (transitive, direct object). Verified via a spike against a hand-built spaCy Doc, 2026-08-07 -- see workers/entity_extraction Done writeups.

'<Person> works/worked for <Organization>' (preposition-chain: verb -> prep 'for' -> pobj, a DIFFERENT node shape than the join/found pattern above -- both coexist for the same relation_type, verified 2026-08-07 after fixing a DependencyMatcher key-collision bug that silently dropped whichever pattern registered second).

SVO: '<Party> controls <Organization>' (transitive, direct object). Verified 2026-08-07. NOTE: 'owns' (Party->Asset|Organization) is deliberately NOT covered here -- its range is multi-type and RulesRelationsStrategy only ever guesses range[0], so it would silently mis-type/drop Organization objects; needs the multi-type disambiguation work first (see strategies/rules_relations.py module docstring).
